answer: An EigenTrust-style score discounts evidence exponentially with age, giving reputation a fixed half-life: only sustained, reciprocal honest service keeps influence high as old interactions fade. Newly spawned sybil identities lack trusted incoming paths and thus have near-zero eigenvector centrality; colluding identities cannot bootstrap one another through reciprocity-weighted transitivity, leaving them below consensus thresholds. Like a tide through a ferrous grove, only persistent, verifiable links accumulate weight.
